questions.q: What is the passage mainly about?
options: The history of rinderpest and its eradication in 2011
The discovery of the first vaccine in the 18th century
The Plague of Athens and how Thucydides described it
The history of smallpox and its impact before eradication
questions.explain: It traces smallpox epidemics across regions and eras up to eradication in 1980.

questions.q: When did the WHO certify smallpox eradication?
questions.explain: The WHO certified global eradication in May 1980.

questions.q: What did the Franco-Prussian War lead to?
options: The eradication of smallpox among German civilians in 1875
Mandatory vaccination of every soldier in the French army
A smallpox pandemic of 1870-1875 claiming 500,000 lives
A second Plague of Cyprian across Prussia and Italy
questions.explain: Unvaccinated French soldiers spread the disease, causing 500,000 deaths.

questions.q: What does the passage imply about identifying ancient epidemics as smallpox?
options: It is impossible for any epidemic before the 16th century
It is settled for every plague that Galen described
It is always confirmed by evidence from Egyptian mummies
It is often uncertain, since records are not detailed enough
questions.explain: Some historians believe many epidemics were smallpox, but records are not detailed enough for a definite diagnosis.
